output.contract_title: Vendor Procurement Agreement with Enterprise Partner 002 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Each party's maximum aggregate liability shall be strictly limited to the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding twelve (12) months.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Payment terms shall not exceed Net 45 days from receipt of undisputed invoice.

recommended_requirements.description: Late payment penalties should not exceed 1.5% per month.

ambiguities_in_policy: Definition of "receipt of undisputed invoice" – timing of when an invoice is considered undisputed is not specified.
Whether "Net 45 days" refers to calendar days or business days is unclear.
The phrase "Late payment penalties should not exceed 1.5% per month" does not clarify if the cap is applied per individual month of delay or as a cumulative maximum over the entire overdue period.
Method of calculating the 1.5% penalty (simple vs. compound interest) is not defined.

mappings.notes: Clause requires payment within 30 days, which is within the Net 45 maximum stipulated by the policy.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is not defined, leaving uncertainty about payment obligations when a dispute arises and no dispute resolution mechanism is referenced.
Absence of a process for handling disputed invoices may cause cash‑flow interruptions and administrative overhead.

Liability is capped at the total fees paid in the preceding twelve months, which may be insufficient to cover potential indirect, consequential, or statutory damages, exposing the non‑paying party to disproportionate risk.
A 30‑day notice period for termination for convenience may not provide adequate time for transition planning, especially for services with longer implementation cycles.
The renewal provision does not specify a maximum number of renewals or an end‑date, creating an open‑ended term that could extend indefinitely without renegotiation.
The clause references "notice of non‑renewal" but does not define acceptable method of delivery (e.g., email, certified mail), leading to potential disputes over whether proper notice was given.

inconsistencies.description: Both the termination clause (30 days notice for convenience) and the renewal clause (30 days notice of non‑renewal) use the same notice period but serve conflicting purposes; a party could give a termination notice while also providing a renewal/non‑renewal notice, creating ambiguity about whether the agreement continues or ends.

The liability cap limits aggregate liability to the total fees paid in the preceding twelve months. If the agreement is terminated early under the termination clause, fees paid may be minimal or zero, effectively reducing liability to zero, which may be inconsistent with the intent to provide a meaningful liability limitation.
